title: Samsung’s Memory Chip Demand Leaves Elon Musk Searching for Answers
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Samsung Electronics reportedly turned down Elon Musk’s proposals to secure a long-term supply of memory chips, highlighting the growing bargaining power of semiconductor manufacturers amid surging artificial intelligence demand.
Samsung Rejects Musk’s Proposals​According to Capital Group portfolio manager Carl Kawaja, Musk initially proposed a long-term purchasing commitment to secure memory chips for Tesla.

Kawaja recounted the conversation during a conference in June 2026, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong reportedly indicated that competing customers had submitted similar proposals, prompting Musk to offer financial guarantees supporting the construction of additional semiconductor manufacturing facilities.

However, the revised offer reportedly failed to persuade Samsung. Neither Samsung nor Capital Group commented on the account, while Tesla did not respond to requests for comment.
AI Boom Strengthens Memory Chip Suppliers​The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has intensified competition for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other semiconductor memory products.

Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology are benefiting from increasing demand as technology companies expand their data center operations.

The supply shortage has also strengthened manufacturers’ negotiating positions, with customers increasingly facing multiyear purchasing commitments and substantial upfront payment requirements.
Tesla’s Existing Samsung Partnership Remains Separate​The reported rejection is unrelated to Samsung’s existing $16.5 billion semiconductor manufacturing agreement with Tesla.

Announced in July 2025, that agreement covers the production of Tesla’s next-generation AI6 processors at Samsung’s Texas manufacturing facility and extends through 2033.

The distinction is significant because manufacturing custom processors and securing dedicated memory chip supplies involve different commercial arrangements.

As global investment in artificial intelligence continues to accelerate, competition for semiconductor components is expected to remain intense. Musk’s reported difficulties illustrate how even the technology industry’s most influential executives face substantial procurement challenges, potentially affecting product development timelines, infrastructure expansion plans and manufacturing costs across multiple industries.
